key_claims: Poor sleep quality was significantly associated with a higher risk of anxiety in Chinese empty-nest older adults.
Short sleep duration was an independent risk factor for anxiety, but long sleep duration showed no significant association.
Physical exercise mediated the relationships of sleep quality and long sleep duration with anxiety.
Social participation mediated the relationships of both short and long sleep duration with anxiety.
limitations: The study is cross-sectional, so causality cannot be inferred.
Sleep and exercise were self-reported, which may introduce bias.
The sample was limited to Chinese empty-nest older adults, so findings may not generalize to other populations.
what_not_to_say: The study proves that improving sleep quality reduces anxiety risk.
Physical exercise and social participation are effective interventions for anxiety.
Long sleep duration is a risk factor for anxiety.
The study included older adults living with family members.
